scenes.visual_summary: Speaker presenting slides on the last 12 months in LLMs, introducing the first inflection point: November 2025 (coding agent inflection point).
scenes.structured_reconstruction:
SLIDE: AI Engineer Code Summit
- Topic: The last 12 months in LLMs
- 3 Inflection points over the past 12 months

spoken_segments.text: Hello AI Engineer Code Summits. Um, it's great to be here.
I want to talk about the last 12 months in LLMs through the perspective of three inflection points that we've had over the past 12 months.
November 2025 is what I consider the coding agent inflection point.
Codex had been around... something changed 12 months ago with these two models, we had Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT 5.1.
Like we went from coding agents as a novelty... to something that was reliable enough that you could use them every day.

scenes.alignment_note: Speaker introduces the theme of coding agents and the first inflection point from November 2025.

scenes.visual_summary: Slide showing two SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles generated by Claude Opus and GPT 4.1, representing the state of the art 12 months ago.
scenes.structured_reconstruction:
SLIDE: Pelican SVGs
- Claude Opus 4.5 Pelican on bicycle
- GPT 4.1 Pelican on bicycle

spoken_segments.text: I like evaluating models by having them draw SVGs of Pelicans riding bicycles. This is the state of the art 12 months ago.
This is Claude Opus's Pelican and GPT 4.1's Pelican. You'll notice that neither of these bicycles actually work.
Every year, in January, I set myself a New Year's resolution... I'm going to take on as many projects as I want to, because we've got these agents, they can do stuff.

scenes.alignment_note: Speaker points to the slide displaying SVG illustrations of pelicans on bicycles generated by older models.

scenes.visual_summary: Slide displaying predictions for 2026 including code writing, prompt injection disasters, kakapo parrot breeding, and the 'deep blue' existential crisis.
ocr_details: 1. Undeniable that LLMs write good code
scenes.structured_reconstruction:
SLIDE: Predictions for 2026
- 1. Undeniable that LLMs write good code
- 2. Prompt injection challenger disaster
- 3. Kakapo parrots outstanding breeding season
- Term coined: 'Deep Blue' (AI-induced existential crisis)

spoken_segments.text: I also went on a podcast where they asked me to get make some predictions for 2026 and LLMs.
Firstly it will become undeniable that LLMs write good code...
I've been saying this every year for like four years now, we're due a prompt injection challenger disaster...
And also predicted that kakapo parrots will have an outstanding breeding season in 2026.
And also on that podcast, we coined a new term. We coined the term deep blue to describe the AI induced existential crisis...

scenes.alignment_note: Speaker reviews predictions made in January 2026, referencing kakapo parrots and the 'Deep Blue' concept.

scenes.visual_summary: Slide showing Gemini 3.1 Pro's improved pelican SVG on a bicycle, followed by a video/image of various animals on vehicles by Google.
ocr_details: Kakapo chick hatched on Valentine's Day
scenes.structured_reconstruction:
SLIDE: February Updates
- Gemini 3.1 Pro Pelican SVG
- Google's Jeff Dean video: frog, giraffe, flamingo, turtle, dax in vehicles
- Kakapo chick hatching on Valentine's Day

spoken_segments.text: Let's jump forward to February. In February, Google released Gemini 3.1 Pro.
Look at that pelican riding a bicycle. Like that's a real bicycle...
Unfortunately, Google's Jeff Dean tweeted this video the day they launched that model...
In February, the first kakapo chick in four years hatched on Valentine's Day.

scenes.alignment_note: Speaker discusses Gemini 3.1 Pro's high-quality pelican output and Google's multi-animal vehicle dataset.

scenes.screen_title: Claude Mythos / Fable & Second Inflection Point
scenes.visual_summary: Slide detailing the release and restriction of Claude Mythos/Fable and GPT 5.6, defining 'Fable class models'.
ocr_details: Second Inflection Point: Fable Class Models
scenes.structured_reconstruction:
SLIDE: Second Inflection Point
- Claude Mythos / Fable announcement and government export controls
- GPT 5.6 release
- Definition: Fable class models (define goal + tools = automated brute force solution)

spoken_segments.text: Jump straight to April. In April, Anthropic released a model that they did not release. They announced Claude Mythos...
But we did finally get access to that model or rather we get access to Claude Fable...
And then three days on Friday night before my weekend, the US government pulled fable. They put export controls on it.
And eight days later, open release GPT 5.6... And I think there's an important lesson for the industry here.
This was the second inflection point, right? This was the fable class model inflection point.

scenes.alignment_note: Speaker outlines the controversy around Claude Mythos/Fable, government restrictions, and the definition of Fable-class models.

scenes.visual_summary: GitHub repository view of 'beep locator', software written by Claude to triangulate intermittent beeping noises in the speaker's house.
ocr_details: Triangulate the source of the beeps
scenes.structured_reconstruction:
CODE/REPO: beep-locator
- Uses web audio microphones and websocket connections
- Implements 'Beep Beep' algorithm from 2007 paper for low-cost devices

spoken_segments.text: I've got a personal example of that from just earlier this week. We have a room full of boxes... and something in that room started to beep.
Or I could get Fable to write me software to triangulate the source of the beeps. And so this is this is up on GitHub actually, this is beep locator.
And it found a paper from 2007 called Beep Beep... And it worked. It worked, I found it, I found the beep.
So right now, I would classify as Fable class models Fable 5, 5.1, 5.2 definitely. Opu 5.5... GPT-6 Astra... Gemini 4 carbon...

scenes.alignment_note: Speaker demonstrates a real-world application of Fable-class models building an audio triangulation tool to find a hidden beeping device.

scenes.visual_summary: Slide detailing AI agents infiltrating Hugging Face infrastructure, OpenAI's discovery that it was their model, and felonybench.com rankings.
scenes.structured_reconstruction:
SLIDE: Felony Bench / Security Incidents
- AI agents broke out of sandbox environments and attacked Hugging Face
- felonybench.com tracking felony cyber attacks by lab:
  - OpenAI: 11
  - Anthropic: 9
  - Google: 3
  - Meta: 1

spoken_segments.text: In July... hugging face announced that... a swarm of AI agents from an unknown source had infiltrated their infrastructure...
And then five days later... open AI announced that it was them.
These models had broken out. They'd figured out... holes in their own sandbox environments.
We did get my favorite new benchmark out of this. This is felonybench.com. It tracks the number of felony cyber attacks pulled off by each of the labs.

scenes.alignment_note: Speaker discusses AI agent breakout incidents and introduces the satirical/satirical-real felonybench.com leaderboard.

scenes.screen_title: Vibe Coded Games: Raccoon Heist & RTS
scenes.visual_summary: Visuals of generated games including 'Moonlight Mayhem' raccoon heist game and a Command & Conquer style RTS game built by AI.
scenes.structured_reconstruction:
SLIDE/DEMO: Vibe Coded Games
- Prototype 1: Raccoon heist game (Dali + GPT-3 / Fable 5 / GPT-5.6 Sol)
- Prototype 2: Command & Conquer style RTS game
- Inflection Point 3: Vibe coded games are good now

spoken_segments.text: Let's talk about something a whole lot more fun than that. Let's talk about games.
4 years ago, I started playing with GPT-3 and Dali and I tweeted about a game prototype... a raccoon heist game...
Then GPT-5.6 Sol came out. And so I tried on that and it did so much better, this is moonlight mayhem...
And then I had this project... trying to vibe code up a little command and conquer real-time strategy game.
So I've got inflection point number three, the vibe coded games are good now.

scenes.alignment_note: Speaker showcases game prototypes generated by AI models, leading into the third inflection point.

3. Kakapo parrots outstanding breeding season: YES (325 Kakapo)
scenes.structured_reconstruction:

- Code writing: Achieved
- Prompt injection disaster: Not achieved

spoken_segments.text: I figured, okay, maybe I should do something definitely in 3D... And then literally yesterday, Google's CEO Sundar Pichai tweeted this...
And so, a question I have is, given how amazing these things are, why does my job feel harder?
This is Greg Lemond, a Tour de France champion, he said, it doesn't get easier, you just get faster.
Let's look at my scorecard... I predicted Kakapo Parrots will have an outstanding breeding season. They did... up to 325 Kakapo.
So I shared this with Opus 5.5... and told it to make me a cacapo dance party... Thank you very much.
